## **Compound IQ: Product Run Thru**

  

Sep 11, 2026

[Lauren Perkins](mailto:ventures@designthefuture.studio) <ginarooksnp@gmail.com> <info@unscripted-health.com> <sshamber01@gmail.com> <anilaconikunicklos@gmail.com>

  

Software demonstration and workflow review with feature feedback

  

## **Software Development and Technical Architecture**

  - Lauren and Sam developed the initial HIPAA-compliant functional medicine platform prototype in approximately 6 weeks.
  - Sam utilized a sophisticated AI-driven development stack to accelerate coding and documentation.
  - The platform incorporates role-based access control for medical assistants, clinicians, and clinic administrators.

  

## **Clinical Interface and User Experience Feedback**

  - Gina recommended relocating the medication search bar to the top of the interface for improved accessibility.
  - The team discussed adding dedicated interface buttons to manage, save, and edit medication favorites and protocols.
  - Gina advised implementing selection menus for common dosages to increase efficiency and reduce manual entry errors.
  - Gina proposed restricting the default provider view to the logged-in user to prevent misattribution of orders.
  - The platform aims to provide pricing and margin transparency for compound pharmacy orders.

  

## **Strategic Planning and Product Roadmap**

  - The group planned to demo competitor platforms Vital and Scripts to analyze their workflows and identify functionality gaps.
  - Future development will prioritize building support for complex titration schedules directly into the prescription workflow.
  - Lauren explored creating a patient-facing view to enable informed decision-making on treatment protocols.

  

## **Prescription Workflow and Titration Logic**

  - Lauren and Gina discussed transitioning away from creating 'fake prescriptions' for titration schedules in favor of a protocol-driven approach.
  - Lauren proposed a system that automatically calculates the total medication quantity required based on a defined titration protocol to simplify pharmacy fulfillment.
  - Gina noted that, as an interim workaround, generating separate prescriptions for each month of a patient's titration schedule remains a potential operational option.

  

## **Platform User Experience and Interface**

  - Gina identified the built-in drug interaction checker as a significant differentiator and advantage over legacy systems like Lifile.
  - Anila and Lauren reviewed the interface, noting that while the platform is intuitive, terminology like 'Canban' may require more accessible labeling for clinical users.
  - The team assessed the current dashboard navigation, agreeing that visual clarity and direct access to categorized orders (e.g., pending payments) are critical for efficiency.

  

## **Strategic Market Growth and Positioning**

  - Lauren proposed focusing on 'longevity-focused' patients (athletes, executives) as a high-value customer segment, alongside the existing weight loss focus.
  - Lauren suggested a strategy of acquiring or partnering with established, antiquated platforms to leverage their existing customer bases and replace legacy technology.
  - Targeting IV clinics was identified as a potential pilot use case to quickly move from testing to active product usage.

  

## **Practice Management and Clinical Compliance**

  - Anila proposed developing a practice management dashboard to track key business metrics, including daily script volume and profit margins.
  - Anila clarified that physician assistants and nurse practitioners can prescribe controlled substances, provided they hold the necessary licensure.

  

## **Next steps**

  - \[Gina Rooks, Sam Shamber\] Review Competitors: Perform a demonstration of Vital and Scripts platforms to analyze competitor workflows and identify functionality gaps.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Add Favorites Feature: Develop the interface capability to add and modify saved protocol favorites and allow users to save specific dosages as presets.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Restrict Provider View: Modify the user interface to automatically default the order to the logged in clinician and remove the ability for providers to select other users.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Standardize Dosing: Implement a selection menu for common medication doses to enable quick access to frequently used prescription amounts.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Move Search Bar: Relocate the medication search bar to the top of the interface to improve accessibility.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Distribute Access: Email the site link, usernames, and passwords to the team for platform testing.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Add Interface Buttons: Add distinct interface buttons for favorites and protocols to the prescription view.
  - \[The group\] Coordinate Demos: Coordinate and schedule demo sessions to evaluate vital and script workflows.
  - \[Anila Coniku-Nicklos\] Verify Prescribing Rules: Research and verify the specific prescribing regulations for physician assistants and nurse practitioners.
  - \[Anila Coniku-Nicklos\] Conduct Interviews: Conduct design thinking interviews with 10 to 30 functional medicine providers to gather user feedback.
  - \[Gina Rooks\] Test Platform: Explore the platform interface to identify potential improvements and document findings.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Refine Dashboard: Improve visual clarity and include business metrics such as script volume and profit margins.
  - \[Sam Shamber\] Design Prescription Workflow: Develop a system that supports titration protocols and refill functionality.
  - \[Lauren Perkins, Gina\] Capture Manual Workflow: Screen share the current process of ordering prescriptions for better software development insight.
  - \[Lauren Perkins\] Share Meeting Notes: Forward the transcript and notes to Sam Shamber.
  - \[Anila Coniku-Nicklos\] Review Square Payments: Evaluate the Square payment interface for potential features to integrate.
